chapter: New Orleans clarinetists and Steve Lewis
title: Reading musicians versus the rag-down players
summary: Reading musicians seldom came around to hear the hot players, who differed in style; Steve Lewis was always there.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, what about those guys like him, the reading guys? Did they come around much and listen to the real, uh, rag-down jazz musicians?

Well, they used to come around occasionally. They didn't come too often. They was kind of a set of fellows that, uh, they didn't think he was doing right. That's what they, that was their idea, by the way.
They thought, they thought music was the only way.

Only way, yeah. Mm-hmm. So they didn't care too much about our style of playing, and they didn't come around too much. Now, P. Ron used to be around often, him. P. Ron used to come often, you couldn't keep Steve Lewis away from that, him. Steve was just an addict to music.
